audit.whatIsWrong: Level 2 is marked Singed and Level 6 is marked Skill, but the page's own why-lines say Body Slam gives him a real engage at 2 and that Explosive Cask hard-counters the chase at 6.
audit.why: Two rows disagree with the prose. The rest of the chart is right for a 55.13% matchup.
audit.corrected: Level 2 and Level 6 both go to Gragas; the other five rows stand.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike names Insanity Potion only as roam cover and never says what it does to Gragas; Explosive Cask carries no cooldown number.
audit.why: Happy Hour heals Gragas every time he casts, and Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds — that is the direct answer to his sustain and it appears nowhere on the page. Explosive Cask is 100/85/70s.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds against Happy Hour at 6; Cask 100s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive's grounding is never mentioned. The page only ever describes Body Slam dashing through or over the glue.
audit.why: Mega Adhesive grounds, and grounding shuts off dashes. Body Slam (14/13.5/13/12.5/12s, 600 range) is Gragas's only dash and his only escape from the poison. Thrown in front of him he dashes across it; dropped under his feet it stops the cast entirely — the page taught the first half and omitted the second.
audit.corrected: Glue under his feet grounds Body Slam; Fling into the glue roots.

audit.whatIsWrong: The cooldown block names Body Slam but gives no number, and Explosive Cask is not listed as a tracked cooldown despite the prose saying to track it.
audit.why: Body Slam 14s at rank 1, Cask 100s at rank 1, Barrel Roll 10s at 850 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[1] tells the player to stack MR against 'his Q sustain pool and Dark Horse AP'.
audit.why: 'Dark Horse AP' is not an item, a rune or an ability. The real reason to buy MR is Barrel Roll's 850-range poke and Drunken Rage's empowered auto.

edits.before: Fling + glue starts punishing anyone who chases. Only take the trade when Gragas's Body Slam is down.
edits.after: Body Slam is live at 2 and it crashes onto you across the glue — bait the dash, then commit nothing.

edits.before: Ult-ghost-proxy is a macro weapon — you win by farming where he is not. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Explosive Cask (100s at rank 1) knocks you off the chase and resets the gap — track its cooldown exactly like Body Slam and never run at him blind.

edits.before: Rylai's Crystal Scepter is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: Rylai's plus glue under his feet: grounded, Body Slam will not cast and he has no way out of the cloud.

edits.after: Glue under his feet grounds Body Slam — the dash will not cast. Fling him into it for the root.

edits.before: His engage. Keep moving. Only engage once it is down or baited.

edits.after: Stack MR (Negatron into Force of Nature) early so Barrel Roll's 850-range poke never threatens your HP bar

edits.before: Body Slam is live and it launches Gragas through your Mega Adhesive before the root triggers, giving him a real engage and W damage reduction to win the trade; respect the dash and do not overcommit.
edits.after: Body Slam is live and he can dash across your glue before it lands, giving him a real engage plus Drunken Rage's damage reduction — bait the 14-second dash into thin air and commit nothing.

edits.before: Without Rylai's Crystal Scepter his Body Slam still lets him hop out of your poison before it stacks; with Rylai's the slow triggers the instant he lands and he cannot Body Slam away cleanly — the kite machine fully coheres.
edits.after: Without Rylai's his Body Slam simply hops him out before the poison stacks; with Rylai's the slow bites the instant he lands, and Mega Adhesive under his feet grounds the dash entirely — he has no way out of the cloud.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are a calculated farming window — proxy behind his wave when you can, keep Poison Trail ticking on his casters, and bank the EXP lead that pays off at 6. Do not force all-ins while Body Slam is up; wait for the dash to be on cooldown before committing Fling. Level 6 temporarily flips: Explosive Cask is a hard counter to your run-at-him pattern because it knocks you away and resets the chase, so treat his ultimate the same way you treat Body Slam — a cooldown to track, not ignore. Insanity Potion is your answer: activate it before he can Cask you out, use the movement speed to close before he repositions, and abuse the stat dump (bonus MR blanks a chunk of his AP burst) to win the sustained trade he cannot escape once his Cask is spent.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are a calculated farming window — proxy behind his wave when you can, keep Poison Trail ticking on his casters, and bank the EXP lead that pays off at 6. Do not force all-ins while Body Slam is up; wait for the 14-second dash to be spent before committing Fling. Level 6 temporarily flips: Explosive Cask is 100 seconds at rank 1 and hard-counters your run-at-him pattern because it knocks you away and resets the chase, so treat it exactly like Body Slam — a cooldown to track, not ignore. Insanity Potion is your answer: it makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds, which cuts the Happy Hour healing he collects off every cast, and the movement speed lets you close before he repositions. Once his Cask is spent, glue under his feet and he cannot Body Slam out of the trade.

notes: Two chart rows flipped as one group to match the page's own prose. The grounding interaction was completely absent: the page repeatedly said Body Slam goes through the glue, which is true if you throw it in his path, but never that glue dropped under his feet grounds the dash and traps him. Also added the Happy Hour / Insanity Potion Grievous Wounds answer, which was missing, and removed 'Dark Horse AP', which is not a real item, rune or ability. UNVERIFIED and left alone: whether Explosive Cask's knockback can be Flash-buffered or whether Body Slam can be cast the same frame the glue lands — needsResearch is empty.
